chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Abu Ismail al-Sarraj, from Harun, from Harun ibn Kharrajah, who said:
I mentioned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) a man from our companions, and I praised him well. So he said to me: 'What is the status of his Salat (prayer)?'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Imam ask about prayer when a companion was praised?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) shifts the focus from general social praise to the specific metric of *Salat* (ritual prayer), highlighting its status as the fundamental differentiator of true piety in Shia jurisprudence. This reflects the scholarly emphasis that while other virtues are commendable, the consistency and quality of one's connection with God through prayer serve as the primary indicator of spiritual standing and religious integrity.
